      "partial_result": "# Critique of the layer-26 MLP proposal after the identity-coverage KILL (master 088181ee, read-only)\n\n**Verdict:** the KILL doesn't identify a responsible layer, but the evidence now points below the readout. Moving to the encoder is reasonable. As specified, though, the proposal is not yet identifiable. It probably can't meet its own cost gate unless it caches the layer-26 inputs, which it currently forbids. One engineering probe is justified, provided its first job is to measure that cost.\n\n## Evidence that bears on which layer is responsible\n\n- From the receipt's per-query R1 vectors, 47 of the control's 55 errors are shared by the source, concat, control and candidate arms. All four arms together miss 75 queries. Readout variants only swap 8\u201314 queries at the edges: candidate vs control is 4 gained / 4 lost, and vs source it is 16 / 7. The core never moves.\n- The identity-coverage KILL changed the data and left the readout family fixed. It says nothing about encoder vs readout. Its AP gain of +0.0016 is a mean over 143 queries that improved and 225 that got worse.\n- The earlier \"last-MLP\" attempt in `scripts/train_siglip2_nearest_ranking.py` never tested the encoder:\n  - Its readout detaches the features (`prototype_residual_readout` `:70/:76`).\n  - Its gradient checks (`:1436`, `:1463`) only require gradients that exist and are finite, so zero gradients pass.\n  - Its `all_four_updated` flag is satisfied by AdamW weight decay alone.\n  - So layer 26 has not been tested yet, either positively or negatively.\n\n## BLOCKERS\n\n**B1 \u2013 The cost gate is probably infeasible under the stated constraints (\u22641.5\u00d7, no token cache, no cap increase).**\n- Allowed extra core time is 1.5 \u00d7 101.582 \u2212 101.582 = 50.79 s. That is 0.397 s per update, or 3.10 ms per anchor-view (128 \u00d7 64 \u00d7 2 views = 16,384). It has to cover pixel regeneration, the prefix forward, the layer-26 MLP and attention-pooling backward, and integrity checks.\n- Measured on the same four tensors, the nearest-ranking mechanics run (`nearest-ranking-mechanics-control-v1/original.log:33-59`) took about 0.81 s per B64 update with one view, plus about 2.0 s of `update_integrity` per update.\n- The exporter managed 12,710 FP16 view forwards in 291.5 s, including model load. That is an upper bound of about 23 ms per view.\n- I can't derive a hard lower bound from the receipts, so this is \"likely\", not proven. But nothing measured comes within 2\u00d7 of the allowance.\n- If it fails, that is a design property, not something tuning can fix. The only exact way out is a constraint change for you (the operator) to decide:\n  - Only the layer-26 MLP changes, and the augmentation seeds are fixed (179081 + ordinal). So the input to the MLP sub-block is a deterministic, finite set of tensors, and caching it is lossless.\n  - That is precisely the \"token cache\" you excluded. Its size is about 3.7 GB per view in FP16. Fitting it under 8 GiB host / <10 GB CUDA is unmeasured.\n\n**B2 \u2013 Training and evaluation don't use the same encoder on both sides.**\n- Anchors would go through the updated encoder; the gallery stays as frozen cached rows. On top of that, the MSE pulls anchors toward prototypes built from frozen features.\n- That is backward-compatible training (Shen et al., CVPR 2020) of a query-side encoder, not training a shared embedding.\n- Before any TRAIN run you have to declare how the selection panel is scored:\n  - **Asymmetric** (re-encode queries with the update, keep the cached gallery): this matches training. The serving consequence is that the gallery must never be re-indexed with the updated encoder.\n  - **Symmetric** (re-encode both sides): the objective never saw a moving gallery, so a KILL can't be interpreted.\n- Either way, no evaluation path exists that re-encodes the selection panel through the update. The public inference API also takes features, not pixels.\n\n**B3 \u2013 The two arms aren't paired at step 0.**\n- The cached rows were produced with FP16 autocast on CUDA (`pooler_output.float()`, exporter `:901`). The helper is FP32 only for the raw \u2190 features segment.\n- With a zero update, live anchor features won't reproduce the cached rows exactly. So the trainer's existing initial checks (`train_siglip2_identity_diversity.py:1524`, raw vs T within 1e-5/1e-6; `:1528`, gallery vs V) will either fail or have to be weakened. Weakening them is a change to the gate.\n- The precision recipe is also undecided: the nearest trainer used FP16 autocast, loss scaler 128 and clip 1; the identity trainer uses none of these.\n\n**B4 \u2013 Optimizer settings for the four tensors aren't specified.**\n- The identity trainer uses AdamW lr 1e-4, wd 0.05.
